subject: ss-cardiology
title: Diseases of the Aorta: Aneurysms and Acute Syndromes

steps.tx: The **Stanford classification** categorizes acute aortic dissections based on involvement of the ascending aorta into **Type A** involving the ascending aorta requiring emergency surgery, and **Type B** confined to the descending aorta managed medically unless acute ischemic or vascular complications develop.
steps.say: The Stanford classification categorizes acute aortic dissections based on involvement of the ascending aorta into Type A involving the ascending aorta requiring emergency surgery, and Type B confined to the descending aorta managed medically unless acute ischemic or vascular complications develop.

left.title: Stanford Type A Dissection
points: Involves ascending aorta (regardless of tear origin)
Mortality 1% to 2% per hour if untreated
Complicated by tamponade, acute AR, coronary malperfusion
Mandatory immediate open surgical replacement

right.title: Stanford Type B Dissection
points: Confined to descending aorta distal to left subclavian
Initial management is medical anti-impulse therapy
TEVAR indicated for complicated type B dissection
Lower early mortality than type A dissection

steps.tx: Axial and coronal contrast views show a thin flap crossing the ascending aorta that splits flow into bright true and darker false channels. The tear sits above the valve in the ascending segment, matching **Stanford** **ascending** disease in the lesson. That label matters because ascending involvement demands emergency **surgery** rather than tablets alone to avert rupture or tamponade.
steps.say: The scans show an intimal flap in the ascending aorta with separate true and false lumens seen in two planes. Because the ascending segment is involved, the case fits Stanford Type A in the lesson. That distinction drives care since Type A needs emergency open repair while uncomplicated descending disease starts with medical control. Use the two views to trace the flap and name each lumen.

vis.alt: Paired axial and coronal CT views show an ascending aortic flap separating true and false lumens.
vis.caption: CT shows ascending dissection flap with true and false lumens. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Initial medical management** of acute aortic dissection targets heart rate < **60** bpm and systolic blood pressure between **100** and **120** mmHg using intravenous beta-blockers such as esmolol or labetalol to decrease aortic wall **shear stress** (dP/dt). Vasodilators are added only after heart rate control is established.

Vasodilators are added only after heart rate control is established.

nodes.label: Acute Aortic Dissection Confirmed on CT Angiography
Start IV Beta-Blocker (Esmolol / Labetalol): Target HR < 60 bpm
Type A -> Emergency OR; Uncomplicated Type B -> ICU Care

steps.tx: **Intramural hematoma** arises from spontaneous rupture of aortic media **vasa vasorum** without an identifiable intimal tear on imaging, appearing on noncontrast CT as a hyperdense, crescentic thickening of the aortic wall without flow in a false lumen. Ascending aortic involvement mandates emergency surgical replacement.

Ascending aortic involvement mandates emergency surgical replacement.

left.title: Type A Intramural Hematoma
points: Involves ascending aortic wall
High rate of progression to overt dissection or rupture
Emergency median sternotomy surgical replacement
Noncontrast CT is essential for visualization

right.title: Type B Intramural Hematoma
points: Confined to descending thoracic aorta
Initial medical therapy with strict blood pressure control
TEVAR indicated for progression, expansion, or pain
Serial CT surveillance at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months

steps.tx: **Penetrating atherosclerotic ulcer** occurs when deep ulcerating atheromatous plaque erodes through the **internal elastic lamina** into the aortic media, typically in elderly hypertensive patients with severe vascular disease. Deep crater formation predisposes to saccular pseudoaneurysm formation or acute transmural rupture. Comprehensive clinical evaluation requires careful correlation with serial electrocardiographic tracings and hemodynamic parameters.

nodes.label: Severe Intimal Atheromatous Plaque in Elderly Smoker
Ulceration Erodes Through Internal Elastic Lamina into Media
High Risk of Saccular Aneurysm or Transmural Rupture
Endovascular Repair (TEVAR) with Stent Graft Exclusion

steps.tx: Elective **surgical threshold** for ascending **Thoracic aortic aneurysm** is recommended at diameter at least **5.5** cm for sporadic aneurysms, at least **5.0** cm for bicuspid aortic valve with risk factors, and at least 5.0 cm (or **4.5** cm with risk factors) for Marfan syndrome. Rapid annual expansion at least 0.5 cm warrants surgical repair.
steps.say: Elective surgical threshold for ascending thoracic aortic aneurysm is recommended at diameter of at least 5 point 5 cm for sporadic aneurysms, at least 5 point 0 cm for bicuspid aortic valve with risk factors, and at least 5 point 0 cm (or 4 point 5 cm with risk factors) for Marfan syndrome. Furthermore, rapid annual expansion of at least 0 point 5 cm warrants prompt surgical repair.

rows: ≥  5.0 cm if undergoing concurrent valve surgery
≥  4.5 cm (family history of dissection, rapid growth)

steps.tx: **Abdominal aortic aneurysm** repair is indicated when maximum **transverse diameter** reaches at least **5.5** cm in men or at least **5.0** cm in women, or with rapid expansion exceeding **0.5** cm in **6** months or **1.0** cm in **1** year. Screening with abdominal ultrasonography is recommended for male smokers aged 65 to 75.
steps.say: Abdominal aortic aneurysm repair is indicated when maximum transverse diameter reaches at least 5 point 5 cm in men or at least 5 point 0 cm in women. Repair is also indicated with rapid expansion exceeding 0 point 5 cm in 6 months or 1 point 0 cm in 1 year. Screening with abdominal ultrasonography is recommended for male smokers aged 65 to 75.

rows: Leak at proximal (IA) or distal (IB) stent attachment
Retrograde filling via lumbar arteries or IMA
Fabric tear or modular component disconnection
Urgent placement of bridging extension endograft
Transudate through graft fabric pores (< 30 days)

steps.tx: **Thoracic endovascular aortic repair** known as **TEVAR** is the preferred treatment for complicated type B acute aortic syndromes, covering the proximal intimal tear to depressurize and remodel the false lumen. Endovascular stent grafting achieves lower perioperative morbidity than open thoracotomy. Comprehensive clinical evaluation requires careful correlation with serial electrocardiographic tracings and hemodynamic parameters.
steps.say: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair known as TEVAR is the preferred treatment for complicated type B acute aortic syndromes, covering the proximal intimal tear to depressurize and remodel the false lumen. Endovascular stent grafting achieves lower perioperative morbidity than open thoracotomy. Comprehensive clinical evaluation requires careful correlation with serial electrocardiographic tracings and hemodynamic parameters.

nodes.label: Complicated Type B Aortic Dissection or Ruptured Ulcer
Percutaneous Femoral Arterial Delivery of Stent Endograft
Deploy TEVAR Covering Primary Proximal Intimal Tear
Depressurize False Lumen & Restore Branch Vessel Flow

edges: Aortic remodeling and true lumen expansion

steps.tx: Aortitis and large-vessel vasculitis predominantly comprise **Takayasu arteritis** affecting young women under **40** years causing pulseless disease, and **Giant cell arteritis** affecting adults over **50** years presenting with temporal arteritis and polymyalgia rheumatica. Systemic corticosteroids represent the primary initial therapy. Comprehensive clinical evaluation requires careful correlation with serial electrocardiographic tracings and hemodynamic parameters.
steps.say: Aortitis and large-vessel vasculitis predominantly comprise Takayasu arteritis affecting young women under 40 years causing pulseless disease, and Giant cell arteritis affecting adults over 50 years presenting with temporal arteritis and polymyalgia rheumatica. Systemic corticosteroids serve as the primary initial medical therapy. Comprehensive clinical evaluation requires careful correlation with serial electrocardiographic tracings and hemodynamic parameters.

left.title: Takayasu Arteritis (Pulseless Disease)
points: Females under 40 years of age
Granulomatous panarteritis of aortic arch and branch ostia
Upper extremity claudication, pulse deficits, asymmetric BP
Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP)

right.title: Giant Cell Arteritis (Temporal Arteritis)
points: Adults over 50 years of age (mean onset 70 years)
Temporal headache, jaw claudication, visual loss risk
Associated with polymyalgia rheumatica in 50%
High-dose systemic corticosteroids prevent permanent blindness
